gen-irish-grover-gf-saira-semi-condensed: Irish Grover stands its lowercase up tall, so words look sturdy, and its strokes flex slightly like bent wire. Saira Semi Condensed holds a constant weight throughout, so paragraphs of it move along without a bump.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-basic: Luckiest Guy shouts with a high mean line and curves and straights poured at a single width. Basic, sans-serif and gently graded from small letters to capitals, gives that noise somewhere quieter to land.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-jaldi: Luckiest Guy is loud and cheerful, with no calligraphic swelling anywhere. Jaldi, a sans-serif with a lofty x-height, a gaping c, and brushed, tightly packed letters, moves along in a friendly, easy-going rhythm.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-momo-trust-display: Loud, cheerful, blunt: Luckiest Guy has no tapering where strokes meet or end. Momo Trust Display, a sans-serif with drifting letters and a generous x-height, reads with a loose ease line after line.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-yantramanav: Luckiest Guy is built for volume, its strokes blunt with no tapering where they meet or end. Yantramanav does the opposite job, packing lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals close together, so text stays tidy.
gen-megrim-fs-chillax: Angular and futuristic, Megrim stands tall on the line. Chillax, a sans-serif with unfinished, pen-lifted curves and moderate height, relaxes everything below the rigid headline, like a blueprint beside a doodle.
gen-megrim-fs-synonym: Every stroke in Megrim ends at the same measured thickness, and its c bends open like a paperclip. Synonym adds dependable, constant ink with generous openings, and that steadiness is what makes the pairing work.
gen-megrim-gf-arsenal: A thread of ink with no swelling: that is Megrim. Arsenal, a sans-serif whose lowercase nearly meets the capitals, moves along as a tight, friendly string, its curves swelling slightly.
gen-megrim-gf-geom: Megrim never lets a thin stroke vanish in glare. Geom adds a lofty lowercase band and friendly modern curves, and that lift against Megrim's angular lines is the strongest thing about the two.
gen-megrim-gf-krona-one: Megrim reads like laser-cut sheet, all one cutting width. Krona One is sans-serif with loosely spaced letters and lowercase standing like cast iron capitals; that hefty mass against Megrim's fine cut is the standout.
